headline: High-risk default interaction: OpenHands can write/egress broadly while Airbyte can ingest business data, creating leakage and cascading-action risk if paired without strict isolation.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airbyte has broad network egress and API access, while OpenHands can use MCP, browsers, shell, and filesystem writes. If Airbyte outputs are routed into OpenHands via shared files or MCP, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. The shared bridge is plausible, but not proven by the profiles alone.
conditions: IF Airbyte exports content into a file or MCP channel that OpenHands reads
IF OpenHands parses that content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of Airbyte outputs into OpenHands
Use a read-only handoff file format with strict schema validation
Separate the agents onto different workspaces
Add a human review step before any OpenHands tool action
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airbyte touches business data and has broad network egress; OpenHands reads and writes runtime files and can send data to a configured model provider. If the same mounted workspace carries business data, OpenHands may transmit it onward during normal operation. This is a default-dangerous leakage path unless the pair is tightly isolated.
conditions: IF business data from Airbyte is mounted into OpenHands' runtime
IF OpenHands forwards file contents to its model provider or MCP servers
mitigations: Keep Airbyte and OpenHands on separate volumes
Remove sensitive datasets from the OpenHands runtime
Disable outbound connectors in OpenHands for the shared workspace
Use synthetic or redacted data for agent-to-agent handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory egress controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airbyte can move data over APIs and OpenHands can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses. If both operate on the same mutable workspace, they can overwrite each other's artifacts or commit conflicting changes. The profiles show overlapping write/egress authority and OpenHands has explicit concurrency scope only within its own runtime, not across the pair.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or git repository
IF Airbyte writes artifacts that OpenHands also edits
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Pause one agent while the other writes shared artifacts
Use git branches with manual merge review
Mount shared data read-only for one side
requires-engineering: add cross-agent locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: OpenHands can act on files and browser/MCP outputs, while Airbyte can produce data and API-derived artifacts. If OpenHands treats Airbyte output as authoritative, it may automate incorrect downstream actions or commits. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so the safer assumption is that unverified outputs can cascade into actions.
conditions: IF OpenHands consumes Airbyte-generated files or records without verification
IF OpenHands uses those records to edit code, commit, or trigger browser actions
mitigations: Require explicit validation before OpenHands acts on Airbyte output
Add checksum or schema checks on transferred artifacts
Limit OpenHands to read-only review of Airbyte outputs
Log every handoff between the agents
requires-engineering: implement a verification gate between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Airbyte touches business data, and OpenHands handles files in a runtime sandbox while sending data to a user-configured model provider. If business data includes regulated or residency-bound records, the pair can create retention or transfer mismatches. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction breach, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated or residency-bound data is placed into the shared runtime
IF OpenHands forwards that data to an external model provider or retains it longer than Airbyte's policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared runtime
Use a provider with approved residency and retention terms
Redact identifiers before handoff
Document retention rules for both agents
requires-engineering: align logging and deletion policies across the pair
